excerpts.text:
Artemis II lifts off from Launch Complex 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on April 1, 2026

The crew arrived at Kennedy Space Center on March 27,[[85]](#cite_note-NASA-2026a-85) and the launch countdown began on March 30.[[86]](#cite_note-86) The mission launched aboard an SLS rocket on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B at 22:35:12 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time") (6:35:12 p.m. [EDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Daylight_Time "Eastern Daylight Time"), local time at the launch site).[[6]](#cite_note-NASA_Launch_Time-6)[[87]](#cite_note-87) It was the first crewed launch from LC-39B since [STS-116](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-116 "STS-116") in 2006.

excerpts.text: **Artemis II** (April 1–11, 2026) flew a crew of four on a [flyby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flyby_(spaceflight) "Flyby (spaceflight)") of the [Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon "Moon"). It was the first crewed flight of the [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")-led [Artemis program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artemis_program "Artemis program"), the only beyond [low Earth orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_Earth_orbit "Low Earth orbit") (LEO) since [Apollo 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_17 "Apollo 17") in 1972, and the only beyond LEO not part of the [Apollo program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_program "Apollo program"). It was also the first crewed flight of the [Space Launch System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Launch_System "Space Launch System") and of the [Orion spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orion_(spacecraft) "Orion (spacecraft)"), which the crew named ***Integrity***.

excerpts.text: Artemis II was crewed by four astronauts: commander [Reid Wiseman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Wiseman "Reid Wiseman"), pilot [Victor Glover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Glover "Victor Glover"), and mission specialist [Christina Koch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Koch "Christina Koch"), all from the [NASA Astronaut Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Corps "NASA Astronaut Corps"), along with mission specialist [Jeremy Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Hansen "Jeremy Hansen") from the [Canadian Astronaut Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Astronaut_Corps "Canadian Astronaut Corps").[[69]](#cite_note-Artemis_Crew-69) On November 22, 2023, [Jenni Gibbons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenni_Gibbons "Jenni Gibbons") was named as Hansen's backup,[[70]](#cite_note-70) and on July 3, 2024, [Andre Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Douglas "Andre Douglas") was named as the backup for the three NASA astronauts.[[71]](#cite_note-Space.com1-71) Glover became the first [person of color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Person_of_color "Person of color"), Koch the [first woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_in_space "Women in space"), Wiseman the oldest person, and Hansen the first non-American to travel around the Moon.

excerpts.text: NASA and SpaceX successfully launched the Crew-11 mission from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Friday, and the spacecraft is now en route to the International Space Station (ISS):

* + NASA and SpaceX launched the Crew-11 mission from Florida and are headed to the ISS on Friday at 11:43 a.m. EDT.
 + The mission includes astronauts from NASA, JAXA, and Roscosmos for a six-month ISS stay.

**CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla.** - NASA and SpaceX successfully launched the Crew-11 mission from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Friday, and the spacecraft is now en route to the International Space Station (ISS).

The four-person crew—NASA astronauts Zena Cardman and Mike Fincke, Kimiya Yui of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), and Oleg Platonov of Roscosmos—boarded SpaceX’s Dragon spacecraft ahead of liftoff on a Falcon 9 rocket at 11:43 a.m.
